catalog_missing.message: No controller catalog was found in {path}. The catalog is built from your own copy of the controller service software and is not shipped with the integration. See the README section "Building the catalog", then restart Home Assistant.

catalog_gone.message: The controller catalog "{name}" is no longer in {path}. Put it back under that name, or remove this entry and add it again to choose another catalog.

catalog_ambiguous.message: There is more than one controller catalog in {path} and this entry does not say which one to use. Remove the entry and add it again; setup will ask which catalog this controller needs.

catalog_outdated.message: The catalog "{name}" has structure version {found}; this integration needs {needed}. Rebuild it with the current compiler and upload it again. See the README section "Building the catalog".

catalog_too_new.message: The catalog "{name}" has structure version {found}, which is newer than the {needed} this integration understands. Update the integration.

catalog_unreadable.message: The catalog "{name}" could not be read as a controller catalog. Rebuild it and upload it again.

text.dst_mismatch:
The controller changes over at {configured}, but {zone} changes at {expected}. Each entry reads month/week/weekday, where week 5 means the last one of the month and weekday 7 is Sunday.

The clock itself is corrected on every poll, so the effect is limited to one poll interval twice a year. To fix it at the source, set the changeover values on the controller, or switch its own changeover off and let Home Assistant keep the time.
